## `CompiledRenderGraph.h`

### `class Muyo::RenderGraph::CompiledRenderGraph`

The compiled, reusable result of RenderGraphBuilder::Build().

Owns the per-node GPU objects and the metadata an executor needs. It is immutable between builds and deliberately holds no per-execution state: barrier bookkeeping, command buffers and in-flight slots belong to whoever executes it.

| Member | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `const std::vector< CompiledRenderGraphNode > & GetNodes() const` | Returns: The compiled nodes, in execution (topological) order. |
| `std::size_t GetNodeCount() const` | Returns: Number of compiled nodes. |
| `void AddNode(CompiledRenderGraphNode node)` | Append a compiled node. Used by RenderGraphBuilder::Build() when compiling. Parameters: `node` - Compiled node to append |
| `void ReserveNodes(std::size_t count)` | Reserve room for count nodes, to avoid reallocation while compiling. Parameters: `count` - Number of nodes expected |
| `void RebuildExecutionPlan(const RenderGraphQueueFamilies &families)` | Recompute the scheduling plan from the current nodes. Called by RenderGraphBuilder::Build() after the nodes are compiled. Parameters: `families` - Queue family indices used to decide which resources cross a queue family |
| `const RenderGraphExecutionPlan & GetExecutionPlan() const` | Returns: The scheduling plan for the current nodes. Read-only during execution. |
| `void Destroy(VkDevice device)` | Destroy every node's GPU objects and clear the node list. Safe to call repeatedly. Parameters: `device` - Device the objects were created on |

### `struct Muyo::RenderGraph::CompiledRenderGraphNode`

GPU objects and execution metadata for one node, produced by RenderGraphBuilder::Build().

Immutable between builds: Execute() only reads it. The definition carries everything a node needs at record time, so it does not point back at the authoring structures.

| Member | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `std::string name` | Node name, used in diagnostics. |
| `std::vector< ResolvedResourceUse > resourceUses` | Resolved resource accesses, used to emit barriers between nodes. |
| `std::vector< VkClearValue > attachmentClearValues` | Clear values for the node's attachments, in attachment declaration order. |
| `bool async` | True when the node opted into the dedicated async compute queue. |
| `VkPipeline pipeline` | Compiled pipeline, or VK_NULL_HANDLE for CPU nodes. Every graph pipeline is created with VK_PIPELINE_CREATE_2_DESCRIPTOR_HEAP_BIT_EXT and layout = VK_NULL_HANDLE (B1b). |
| `bool bOwnsPipeline` | True when this node owns pipeline. False for a pipeline reused from the builder's pipeline cache: Destroy() must then leave it alive, because another node or the next Build still uses it. |
| `bool isRayTracing` | True when this node dispatches a ray tracing pipeline. |
| `std::array< VkStridedDeviceAddressRegionKHR, 3 > sbtRegions` | Shader binding table regions, for ray tracing nodes. |
| `VkExtent2D traceExtent` | Extent the ray tracing trace call is issued over. |
| `std::unordered_map< std::string, uint32_t > heapIndices` | Resource use -> service index, for a heap node. Key is handle#usage. |
| `std::vector< VkPushConstantRange > heapPushRanges` | Push-constant ranges declared by a heap node's shaders; each must be covered by PushData. |
| `QueueType queueType` | Queue the node was compiled for. |
| `VkPipelineBindPoint bindingPoint` | Bind point of the compiled pipeline. |
| `RenderGraphNodeCallback execute` | Records the node's work. |
| `void Destroy(VkDevice device)` | Destroy this node's GPU objects and clear the handles. Safe to call repeatedly. Parameters: `device` - Device the objects were created on |

### `VertexInputLayout Muyo::RenderGraph::ToVertexLayout(VertexType vertexType)`

Map a VertexType to the vertex input layout its pipeline must declare.

A table indexed by the enum, for the reason ToVkIndexed records: a switch made "this type has a layout" a belief, and a value outside the enum left both vectors empty. The pipeline was then created with no vertex input at all, and the failure surfaced at draw time as a validation error far from the value that caused it (issue #178). The table's size is checked against VertexType::COUNT, so adding an enumerator without its layout is a compile error rather than a runtime throw nobody notices.

| Parameter | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `vertexType` | Vertex layout to map. |

**Returns** — The binding and attribute descriptions for that layout.

**Throws**

- `std::invalid_argument` — when vertexType is not one of the enumerators.

### `constexpr VkEnum Muyo::RenderGraph::ToVkIndexed(Enum value, const std::array< VkEnum, N > &table, const char *typeName)`

Map an enum value through a table indexed by its underlying value.

A table rather than a switch because a switch's exhaustiveness was a belief: the seven conversions in this header fell off the end of a non-void function for any value outside the enum, which is undefined behaviour, and -Wreturn-type reported all seven unnoticed (issue #174). Indexing makes the mapping total by construction, and the table's size is deduced from its initialisers and checked against the enum's COUNT: adding an enumerator without adding its mapping, or removing a mapping, is a compile error. The first version of this fix sized each table by COUNT, which made that assertion vacuous - an added enumerator simply extended the array with a zero - and a mutation test caught it.

The bounds check is a runtime check and not an assert, per AGENTS section 3: the value can be falsified by input - a psoDesc a graph user filled in - so it has to survive NDEBUG.

| Parameter | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `Enum` | Enum whose enumerators are contiguous from zero, with a trailing COUNT. |
| `VkEnum` | Vulkan enumerator type the table holds. |
| `N` | Table size, which must equal Enum::COUNT. |
| `value` | Value to map. |
| `table` | One Vulkan enumerator per Enum value, in declaration order. |
| `typeName` | Enum name, used in the exception so the message says which type was wrong. |

**Returns** — The mapped Vulkan enumerator.

**Throws**

- `std::invalid_argument` — when value is not one of the enumerators.

## `PipelineCache.h`

### `class Muyo::RenderGraph::PipelineCache`

A caller-owned cache of VkPipeline objects, shared across render graph builders.

A RenderGraphBuilder caches the pipelines it compiles, but that cache belongs to the builder. Two builders - a second graph, or a builder recreated after a swapchain change - therefore compile identical pipelines independently, and a builder's teardown releases only the pipelines it created. This type moves ownership out of the builder: entries live until Reset() or the cache's own destruction, and a builder that is given one borrows entries instead of owning them.

Inject it through RenderGraphServices::pipelineCache. When the field is null the builder keeps its existing per-builder cache, so a caller that never shares anything needs no extra object.

Lifetime. The cache is device-scoped and must outlive every builder that uses it. It is not safe to destroy it while a builder or a submitted execution still names one of its entries; the device must be idle before the cache is destroyed or Reset() is called. A builder validates that the cache belongs to the same VkDevice at construction, because an entry created on another device is a handle the driver cannot use.

Key. The key is opaque to this type. RenderGraphBuilder builds it from the full pipeline state (the PSODesc, shader content, attachment formats, specialization values and queue type) as a byte string, using the same function as the per-builder fallback, so the two paths cannot disagree about what "the same pipeline" means. Different declarations therefore miss even when they produce compatible drivers state: correctness comes before a higher hit rate.

Threading. One thread at a time, like the builder and the device objects it borrows. The map is not synchronized.

Driver cache. The object also owns a VkPipelineCache, passed to every pipeline creation a builder performs, so the driver can reuse its own compiled state across runs. GetSerializedData() returns the bytes vkGetPipelineCacheData produces; loading and saving a file is the caller's policy, not this type's, and the same is true of deciding where it lives. A PipelineCache created from those bytes starts with the driver's cache loaded and an empty map of VkPipeline handles: the handles are process-local, but the key path is the same on the next run.

| Member | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `PipelineCache(VkRenderDevice *renderDevice)` | Parameters: `renderDevice` - Device the cached pipelines are created on. Must be non-null; it has to outlive the cache, because destroying a cached pipeline goes through its VkDevice Throws: `std::runtime_error` - when renderDevice is null or has no logical device |
| `PipelineCache(VkRenderDevice *renderDevice, std::span< const std::uint8_t > initialData)` | Create a cache with driver data from an earlier GetSerializedData() on the same device. Parameters: `renderDevice` - Device the cached pipelines are created on; same requirements as above; `initialData` - Bytes from GetSerializedData(), or an empty span for a cold cache Throws: `std::runtime_error` - when renderDevice is null or has no logical device |
| `~PipelineCache()` | Destroy every cached pipeline and the VkPipelineCache itself. The device must be idle, and no builder or execution may still refer to an entry - the same requirement as Reset(). |
| `PipelineCache(const PipelineCache &)=delete` | Owns raw Vulkan handles and destroys them, so copying would double-destroy a pipeline. |
| `PipelineCache & operator=(const PipelineCache &)=delete` | Deleted for the same reason as the copy constructor. |
| `PipelineCache(PipelineCache &&)=delete` | Deleted because a moved-from cache would leave the old object with no entries to destroy. |
| `PipelineCache & operator=(PipelineCache &&)=delete` | Deleted for the same reason as the move constructor. |
| `VkPipeline Find(std::string_view key) const` | Parameters: `key` - Byte-string key produced by the builder's full-state pipeline key Returns: The cached pipeline, or VK_NULL_HANDLE when key has no entry. |
| `bool Insert(std::string_view key, VkPipeline pipeline)` | Take ownership of a pipeline and cache it under key. Parameters: `key` - Byte-string key produced by the builder's full-state pipeline key; `pipeline` - Pipeline created on GetDevice(); ownership transfers only on success Returns: True when the entry was stored and is now owned by the cache; false when key was taken. |
| `void Reset()` | Destroy every cached pipeline and clear the map. Safe to call repeatedly. |
| `std::size_t GetPipelineCount() const` | Returns: How many pipelines the cache currently owns. Used by tests and diagnostics to observe reuse across builders; it is not a frame-cost metric. |
| `VkDevice GetDevice() const` | Returns: The logical device the entries were created on. A builder compares this to its own device before borrowing, so a cache shared with the wrong device is a named error. |
| `VkPipelineCache GetVkPipelineCache() const` | Returns: The VkPipelineCache passed to pipeline creation. Never VK_NULL_HANDLE for a live object; the builder passes it to every graphics, compute and ray-tracing create call. |
| `std::vector< std::uint8_t > GetSerializedData() const` | initialData constructor. The device must be idle while this runs: Vulkan requires host access to a VkPipelineCache to be externally synchronized, and a pipeline creation on another thread is the conflict. Returns: The driver's pipeline-cache bytes (vkGetPipelineCacheData), or an empty vector when the driver reports none. |


## `RenderGraphBuilder.h`

### `class Muyo::RenderGraph::IGraphCaptureMarker`

The host's capture-tool marker for a node scope.

A capture backend is host policy, and the graph must not reach one: src/Debug/ScopedMarker.h composes this behaviour for the engine, and the graph used to depend on it just to emit a node marker (#272). A host that wants marker scopes implements this interface around its backend and passes it in RenderGraphServices::captureMarker; without one the graph emits only the Vulkan debug label.

| Member | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `virtual ~IGraphCaptureMarker()=default` | Destroy the marker. The host owns it and must outlive the builder that refers to it. |
| `virtual void Begin(const std::string &name)=0` | Open a marker for a node. Parameters: `name` - Marker name, which is the node's name |
| `virtual void End()=0` | Close the marker opened by the matching Begin. |

Maximum number of shader stages a node may declare (vertex + fragment, or raygen/miss/hit...).

### `class Muyo::RenderGraph::RenderGraphBuilder`

Declares and runs a render graph.

Typical use: RenderGraphBuilderbuilder(RenderGraphServices{.device=device, .resourceAllocator=&allocator, .descriptorHeap=&heap}); builder.AddResource("Color",ImageResourceDesc{.format=...,.extent=...,.usage=...}); builder.ImportResource("Vertices",meshManager.m_pVertexBuffer); builder.AddNode({.nodeName="Opaque",.queueType=QueueType::GRAPHICS,...}); builder.Build(); builder.Execute();

Build() is idempotent for a fixed declaration: it topologically sorts the nodes, allocates graph-owned resources, writes descriptor-heap slots, compiles pipelines and plans barriers. A repeated build reuses the allocations, the compiled pipelines, the descriptor slots and - crucially - the per-slot transient arenas, so a per-frame Build() does not reallocate a graph-owned transient. A changed transient declaration or plan drains every in-flight execution before the old arenas are destroyed; an unchanged plan never drains. Execute() records and submits the frame, splitting work across queues when nodes opt into async compute.

| Member | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `RenderGraphBuilder(const RenderGraphServices &services, uint32_t inFlightCount=1)` | Parameters: `services` - The device, resource allocator and descriptor allocator the graph uses. Each is required; a missing one is reported by name rather than dereferenced later, and the check throws so it survives NDEBUG; `inFlightCount` - How many executions may be in flight at once. The default of 1 serialises them. Above 1, each slot owns its command buffers, root arena and a complete copy of the graph's transients (see GetTransientMemoryPlan()), and imported resources are bound per execution from that slot's descriptor ring. A graph-owned Persistent resource is shared by every execution and is therefore rejected above one slot; a caller that needs per-execution content imports it and re-points the handle between executions (#83) |
| `RenderGraphBuilder(VkRenderDevice *renderDevice, uint32_t inFlightCount=1)` | Convenience: creates the device's VMA-backed resource allocator for renderDevice. Parameters: `renderDevice` - Device used to create pipelines, command buffers and synchronisation; `inFlightCount` - See the services constructor; the default serialises executions |
| `~RenderGraphBuilder()` | Releases the pipelines this builder created and its command buffers. A pipeline borrowed from an injected PipelineCache is not released: that cache owns it and may still serve another builder. |
| `const CompiledRenderGraph & GetCompiledGraph() const` | Returns: The graph compiled by the last successful Build(); empty before the first and after a failed Build. Exposed for diagnostics and tests that inspect the compiled pipelines. |
| `void WaitIdle()` | Block until every submitted execution has completed. Does not record or submit work; use it before reading back an imported resource written by a non-blocking Execute(). |
| `void ReleaseCachedDeviceObjects()` | Release the descriptor slots and the pipelines this builder owns from earlier Builds. Call only when every execution that used them has completed - the app's swapchain recreation does this right after vkDeviceWaitIdle. The next Build recreates what it needs; graph-owned resources are untouched. |
| `RenderGraphBuilder & AddResource(const ResourceHandle &handle, ResourceDesc desc)` | Declare a graph-owned resource. It is allocated at Build() from desc. Parameters: `handle` - Name the graph and the nodes use for it; `desc` - Allocation: buffer size, or image format/extent/usage, plus its lifetime Returns: *this for chaining. Throws: `std::runtime_error` - if desc cannot describe an allocation - a zero count/stride, a zero extent, VK_FORMAT_UNDEFINED, zero mips/layers, or usage == 0 - or if it asks for ResourceLifetime::Imported; use ImportResource for a resource the graph does not own |
| `RenderGraphBuilder & ImportResource(const ResourceHandle &handle, const IGraphResource *resource, VkImageLayout currentLayout=VK_IMAGE_LAYOUT_UNDEFINED)` | Register an externally owned resource (mesh buffers, scene data, TLAS...). Not allocated or freed by the graph. Parameters: `handle` - Name the graph and the nodes use for it; `resource` - The resource; the graph never frees it; `currentLayout` - For an imported image, the layout it is in when an execution begins. The default, VK_IMAGE_LAYOUT_UNDEFINED, promises nothing about its contents: the first node to use it transitions from UNDEFINED, which discards them. A caller importing content produced outside the graph - a scene pass that has not been ported yet, or a capture - passes the layout that content is in, and the graph's first-use barrier transitions from there instead. The graph cannot see the caller's outside writes, so the statement has to stay true for every execution; re-import when the layout changes. A non-UNDEFINED layout on a non-image is rejected Returns: *this for chaining. |
| `std::optional< ResourceDesc > GetResourceDesc(const ResourceHandle &handle) const` | Returns: The allocation description for a graph-owned resource, if any. |
| `const IGraphResource * ResolveResource(const ResourceHandle &handle) const` | Resolve a handle to the resource it names: a transient the graph owns (bound into an aliasing block), one the caller imported, or one the engine's resource manager owns. Parameters: `handle` - Resource handle Returns: The resource, or nullptr when the handle names nothing the graph can see. |
| `const TransientMemoryPlan & GetTransientMemoryPlan() const` | Returns: The last build's transient memory plan: the blocks, their slots, and the two byte totals for one in-flight slot. The builder allocates one copy of this plan per slot, so the graph's total transient memory is reservedBytes * inFlightCount; the plan is shared because every slot binds the same resources at the same offsets. reservedBytes < individualBytes is what sharing memory looks like from outside, and reservedBytes == individualBytes is a legitimate answer for a graph whose transients all overlap in time. Empty before the first build. |
| `void AddNode(const RenderGraphNodeCreateInfo &nodeCreateInfo)` | Declare a node. Throws: `std::runtime_error` - if the name is already used; a resource use names something neither declared with AddResource nor imported; a use's kind or usage does not agree with the resource it names (a sampled-only image bound as STORAGE_IMAGE, an image role on a buffer); a node's shader count does not match its queue type; a non-CPU node has no execute callback; or its attachments resolve to different extents |
| `void AddDependency(const std::string &fromNode, const std::string &toNode)` | Add an ordering edge: toNode runs after fromNode. Throws if either node is unknown or if the edge would create a cycle. |
| `void Build()` | Compile the graph: topological sort, resource allocation, pipeline/descriptor compilation and barrier planning. Call after all resources and nodes are declared. Throws: `std::runtime_error` - for a declaration error, naming the node and resource: a dependency cycle; a transient read with no writer; and anything CompileRenderGraphNode rejects (shader load, specialization ids, buffer range, a missing heap service). docs/RenderGraph.md has the failure index |
| `void Execute()` | Run every node once in execution order, inserting barriers between nodes and synchronising cross-queue handovers. |
| `void SetTraceSink(std::function< void(RenderGraphTrace)> sink)` | Receive a trace of every execution from now on. Parameters: `sink` - Called after each execution completes submission, with that execution's record |
| `void Execute(const RenderGraphExecuteInfo &info)` | Record and submit without waiting for the GPU. With inFlightCount > 1 a second call may record and submit while the first is still in flight; its transients come from its own arena, and its imported resources from its own descriptor ring. The builder is single-threaded: one Execute() must return before the next begins, and Build() must not run concurrently with one. Parameters: `info` - External semaphores to wait on before, and signal after, this execution |
| `std::vector< std::string > GetExecutionOrder() const` | Returns: The node names in dependency (topological) order. |
| `const RenderGraphExecutionPlan & GetExecutionPlan() const` | Returns: The plan the last Build() produced: queue segments and cross-queue transfers. Derived, read-only state, empty before the first Build(). It is what tells a caller whether an async node actually got a cross-queue handover or was serialised on one family. |
| `std::string ToMermaid() const` | Render what Build() compiled as a Mermaid flowchart, without executing anything. Returns: A Mermaid flowchart LR document. |
| `std::string ToDot() const` | Render what Build() compiled as Graphviz DOT, for dot -Tsvg where no browser is involved. Returns: A DOT document. Empty before Build(). |
| `RenderGraphBuilder(const RenderGraphBuilder &)=delete` | The builder owns GPU resources, so copying it is not allowed. |
| `RenderGraphBuilder & operator=(const RenderGraphBuilder &)=delete` | The builder owns GPU resources, so copy-assigning it is not allowed. |
| `RenderGraphBuilder(RenderGraphBuilder &&)=delete` | The builder owns GPU resources, so moving it is not allowed. |
| `RenderGraphBuilder & operator=(RenderGraphBuilder &&)=delete` | The builder owns GPU resources, so move-assigning it is not allowed. |

| `QueueType queueType` | Queue the node runs on. |
| `bool async` | Opt-in: only when set (and queueType == COMPUTE) may the node run concurrently with the graphics queue. Without it the node is recorded on the graphics queue, so no cross-queue work is generated. |
| `std::vector< ResourceUse > resourceUses` | Resources the node reads/writes. |
| `std::vector< std::string > shaderNames` | Shader names for graphics (vert+frag) or compute. |

When queueType == RAY_TRACING these are compiled into a heap-flagged ray tracing pipeline (with a graph-managed shader binding table) and the node automatically issues vkCmdTraceRaysKHR over the extent of its first STORAGE_IMAGE resource. The TLAS, storage image and buffer handles reach the shaders through PushData, like every other heap node. |
| `PSODesc psoDesc` | Graphics pipeline state (ignored for compute/RT). |
| `uint32_t costHint` | Reserved for the future scheduler. |
| `std::vector< VkClearValue > attachmentClearValues` | Optional clear values for the node's attachments, in attachment declaration order. |

### `struct Muyo::RenderGraph::RenderGraphServices`

The services a graph is given, rather than looking up as globals (#53).

The split follows the design document: the graph owns the policy - transient lifetimes, barriers, scheduling, descriptor content - while the mechanism belongs to the host. The device, the memory and the descriptors are the host's, so they arrive by construction. A caller that supplies all three runs a graph without the engine's globals, which is what lets a compute-only consumer use it without the renderer. RenderGraphBuilder(VkRenderDevice*) still fills the other two from those globals for in-tree callers that have not moved, and is marked as the transition rather than the shape.

A host may also supply the shader bytes instead of relying on the graph's file lookup: see shaderSource. The graph owns pipeline creation, so it still compiles the pipelines, but no longer owns the decision of where a shader lives.

| Member | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `VkRenderDevice * device` | Device the graph creates pipelines, command buffers and synchronisation with. Required. |
| `IGraphResourceAllocator * resourceAllocator` | Allocates the graph's declared resources. Required. |
| `DescriptorHeapService * descriptorHeap` | The B-track heap service. Required for every GPU node since B1b; the graph rejects a missing service by name. The descriptor-set allocator is no longer a graph service. |
| `PipelineCache * pipelineCache` | Optional pipeline cache shared by every builder that is given the same instance (#17). |
| `IGraphCaptureMarker * captureMarker` | Optional host capture-tool marker, opened and closed around each node's recorded scope. |
| `ShaderCache * shaderCache` | Optional shader module/reflection cache shared by every builder that is given the same instance (#17). When null, each builder loads and owns its shader modules as before. |
| `const IShaderSourceProvider * shaderSource` | Optional source of every shader a node declares (#292). |

### `std::unordered_map< ResourceHandle, ResourceDesc > ResourceDescRegistry`

Map of every declared resource handle to its allocation description.

### `struct Muyo::RenderGraph::SpecializationValue`

A value supplied for one of a shader's specialization constants.

Its width is deliberately absent: the shader's reflection knows whether the constant is 8, 16, 32 or 64 bits, so the graph takes the width from there. A caller therefore cannot disagree with the shader about the size of its own constant, which is the failure a raw byte array invites.

| Member | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `uint32_t id` | The constant_id the shader declared. |
| `uint64_t value` | Interpreted as the constant's declared width, little-endian. |


## `RenderGraphExecuteInfo.h`

### `struct Muyo::RenderGraph::RenderGraphExecuteInfo`

External synchronization for one execution.

signalSemaphore and signalFence both mean "every queue of this execution has completed". The semaphore is what a present path needs; the fence is host-waitable, so a caller that only wants to know the work is done does not have to submit anything of its own to find out.

Passing neither is legitimate: the executor tracks completion itself with timeline values, and WaitIdle() observes it. Asking for no outward signal therefore costs nothing - in particular it needs no join submission.

The executor's own timelines stay private. A caller that wants to chain executions owns its own timeline and passes it as both signalSemaphore/signalValue here and waitSemaphore/waitValue on the next execution, so the chaining contract does not depend on how the executor lays out its internal counters.

Overlapping executions of the same graph share that graph's resources and are unordered relative to each other unless chained through these semaphores.

| Member | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `VkSemaphore waitSemaphore` | Waited on before this execution's first work - e.g. the swapchain image-acquired semaphore. |
| `uint64_t waitValue` | Value to wait for when waitSemaphore is a timeline semaphore. This is what lets a caller chain one execution onto another's completion: pass the same timeline the earlier execution signalled and the value it signalled. Ignored for a binary semaphore. |
| `VkSemaphore signalSemaphore` | Signalled once all of this execution's queues have completed - e.g. for vkQueuePresentKHR. |
| `uint64_t signalValue` | Value to signal when signalSemaphore is a timeline semaphore. Must be greater than the semaphore's current value, so the default 0 is never valid for one. Ignored for a binary semaphore. |
| `VkFence signalFence` | Signalled once all of this execution's queues have completed. Unlike signalSemaphore this is waitable from the host, and unlike a query it needs no submission of the caller's own. |

### `struct Muyo::RenderGraph::RenderGraphExecutionPlan`

The scheduling plan derived from a compiled graph.

Tells an executor what to run where: which nodes are host-side, how the GPU nodes split into per-queue segments, and which resources cross a queue-family boundary. Derived purely from the compiled nodes and the device's queue families, so it is rebuilt whenever the graph is built and is read-only during execution.

| Member | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `std::vector< std::size_t > cpuNodes` | Compiled node indices that run host-side (QueueType::CPU). They all run before any GPU segment is recorded, and belong to no segment. |
| `std::vector< RenderGraphQueueSegment > segments` | Contiguous per-queue runs of compiled nodes, in execution order. |
| `std::vector< RenderGraphQueueTransfer > transfers` | Resources crossing a queue-family boundary between two segments. |
| `bool IsEmpty() const` | Returns: True when the graph has no GPU work to run. |
| `std::size_t GetSegmentCount() const` | Returns: Number of queue segments. |
| `std::size_t GetTransferCount() const` | Returns: Number of cross-queue transfers. |

### `struct Muyo::RenderGraph::RenderGraphQueueFamilies`

Queue family indices a plan resolves queue keys against.

| Member | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `uint32_t graphics` | Family that runs graphics and ray tracing work. |
| `uint32_t compute` | Family that runs compute work. |

### `struct Muyo::RenderGraph::RenderGraphQueueSegment`

A contiguous run of compiled nodes that executes on one queue.

Segment indices are ranges into CompiledRenderGraph::GetNodes(), so they are stable as long as the graph is not rebuilt.

Segments are split at CPU nodes, so two adjacent segments can share a queue: a [GPU, CPU, GPU] sequence on one queue yields two segments, and therefore two submissions where the pre-split code made one. That is correct (program order on one queue) and adjacent segments with the same queueType need no ownership transfer, so a scheduler is free to merge them into a single submission.

| Member | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `QueueType queueType` | Resolved queue this segment runs on. |
| `std::size_t begin` | First compiled node index (inclusive). |
| `std::size_t end` | One past the last compiled node index. |

### `struct Muyo::RenderGraph::RenderGraphQueueTransfer`

A resource handed from one queue segment to another across a queue-family boundary.

Requires a release barrier when the producer segment ends and an acquire barrier before the consumer segment first touches the resource, plus a semaphore to order the two submissions.

| Member | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `std::size_t producer` | Segment that last used the resource. |
| `std::size_t consumer` | Segment that next uses it. |
| `ResourceHandle handle` | Resource being handed over. |
| `uint32_t producerFamily` | Queue family handing it over. |
| `uint32_t consumerFamily` | Queue family taking ownership. |

## `RenderGraphNodeResource.h`

### `struct Muyo::RenderGraph::BufferRange`

A byte range inside a buffer resource - a view of part of it.

Declared on a ResourceUse to bind only [offset, offset + size), which is what one tensor of a packed weights buffer or a row of a KV cache needs. Without it the whole buffer is bound, which is what every existing caller gets.

The range is resolved at Build(): it is written into VkDescriptorBufferInfo once, so changing it means rebuilding the graph. A base that is only known per execution is a different mechanism, not a different value of this one - see issue #81.

| Member | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `uint64_t offset` | Byte offset from the start of the buffer. |
| `uint64_t size` | Byte length of the range. Must not be zero. |

### `enum QueueType`

Which executor / queue a node runs on. CPU is treated as a queue inside the graph.

A node with QueueType::COMPUTE and RenderGraphNodeCreateInfo::async set may be run concurrently with the graphics queue; every other value is recorded on the graphics queue.

| Value | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `GRAPHICS` | Graphics queue. |
| `COMPUTE` | Compute queue (async only when the node opts in). |
| `COPY` | Transfer work (currently the graphics queue). |
| `RAY_TRACING` | Ray tracing pipeline, dispatched on the graphics queue. |
| `CPU` | Host-side node, executed inline while the graph runs. |
| `COUNT` | Number of queue types; not a valid value. |

### `struct Muyo::RenderGraph::ResolvedResourceUse`

A ResourceUse after the graph has resolved it to concrete barrier state.

Produced by ResolveResourceUse(); mostly consumed internally by RenderGraphBuilder.

| Member | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `ResourceHandle handle` | Name of the resource. |
| `ResourceVersion version` | Write version this use refers to. |
| `ResourceKind kind` | Concrete resource kind. |
| `ResourceIOType io` | Read / write / read-write. |
| `ResourceUsage usage` | Semantic role. |
| `VkPipelineStageFlags2 stages` | Pipeline stages that access the resource. |
| `VkAccessFlags2 access` | Access mask for the resource. |
| `VkImageLayout imageLayout` | Image layout (images only). |
| `VkFormat format` | Optional format (validation / pipeline creation). |
| `VkExtent3D extent` | Optional extent (validation / trace dispatch). |
| `std::optional< BufferRange > bufferRange` | Byte range of a buffer resource bound by the heap descriptor, carried through from the declaration. The barrier path deliberately ignores it - a range is a binding claim, not a claim that two uses touch disjoint bytes, so hazards stay per-resource and conservative. |

### `enum ResourceIOType`

Whether a node reads or writes a resource. Drives barrier generation.

| Value | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `READ` | Read-only access. |
| `WRITE` | Written by a shader (a storage buffer store, an attachment write). |
| `READ_WRITE` | Read and write (e.g. an atomic counter). |
| `TRANSFER_WRITE` | Written by a transfer operation (e.g. vkCmdCopyBuffer). |
| `HOST_WRITE` | Written by the host through a mapping, e.g. BufferResource::SetData or Map()/memcpy. Distinct from `WRITE` because the barrier has to be: a host write's source scope is `HOST`/`HOST_WRITE`, and a shader write's is the shader stages. Declaring one as the other leaves the barrier ordering a write that never happened - and the graph cannot infer it from the node's queue type, because a GPU node that maps a buffer is a documented pattern (`EnsureMappingsReleased` guards it). See #152. |

### `enum ResourceKind`

The concrete Vulkan object kind behind a resource handle.

| Value | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `IMAGE` | A VkImage (render target / storage image). |
| `BUFFER` | A VkBuffer. |
| `ACCELERATION_STRUCTURE` | A VkAccelerationStructureKHR (e.g. a TLAS). |
| `SAMPLER` | A VkSampler. |

### `enum ResourceUsage`

The semantic role of a resource within a node.

Together with ResourceIOType this selects a UsagePolicy (barrier stage/access/layout), and for graphics nodes it also determines how the resource is bound (attachment, vertex buffer...).

| Value | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `SAMPLED` | Sampled texture. |
| `STORAGE_IMAGE` | Read/write storage image. |
| `COLOR_ATTACHMENT` | Color render target. |
| `DEPTH_STENCIL_ATTACHMENT` | Depth/stencil render target. |
| `INPUT_ATTACHMENT` | Input attachment read. |
| `RESOLVE_ATTACHMENT` | Multisample resolve target. |
| `PRESENT` | Final image an external consumer (the presentation engine) reads. |
| `UNIFORM_BUFFER` | Uniform buffer. |
| `STORAGE_BUFFER` | Storage buffer. |
| `VERTEX_BUFFER` | Vertex buffer. |
| `INDEX_BUFFER` | Index buffer. |
| `INDIRECT_BUFFER` | Indirect draw/dispatch buffer. |
| `DRAW_COMMAND_BUFFER` | Draw/draw-count command buffer (written by compute, read by draws). |
| `TRANSFER_SOURCE` | Copy source (vkCmdCopyImageToBuffer, vkCmdCopyBufferToImage, vkCmdCopyBuffer...). Images are moved to VK_IMAGE_LAYOUT_TRANSFER_SRC_OPTIMAL. |
| `TRANSFER_DEST` | Copy, upload, clear or fill destination (vkCmdCopy*, vkCmdClear*Image, vkCmdFillBuffer). One role covers all four because the barrier they need is the same one: the transfer stage, `VK_ACCESS_2_TRANSFER_WRITE_BIT`, and `VK_IMAGE_LAYOUT_TRANSFER_DST_OPTIMAL` for an image - a clear is a transfer write in the specification's own terms, not a colour-attachment one. Which command the node records is its own business; the graph only needs the access. |
| `ACCEL_STRUCTURE` | Top-level acceleration structure (TLAS). |
| `TASK_PAYLOAD` | Mesh shader task payload. |
| `MESH_PAYLOAD` | Mesh shader output payload. |
| `WORKGRAPH_NODE` | GPU work graph node record. |
| `PUSH_CONSTANTS` | Push constants (not resolved as a resource). |

### `uint64_t ResourceVersion`

Monotonic version counter used to track resource writes across nodes.

### `void Muyo::RenderGraph::ValidateBufferRange(const ResourceHandle &nodeName, const ResourceHandle &handle, const BufferRange &range, uint64_t bufferSize, uint64_t requiredAlignment)`

Validate a declared byte range against the buffer it addresses and a device alignment limit.

Free, and taking the alignment as an argument, for two reasons. It has to be callable from both places a buffer is bound into a descriptor, which are different classes. And the failure modes are worth testing on any machine: how much alignment a driver demands is a property of that device (minStorageBufferOffsetAlignment may be far larger than the 4 bytes this machine requires), while a free function with the limit passed in tests the rule without needing the device that exhibits it.

Both checks exist because neither is caught where the mistake is made: an out-of-range range reads or writes the wrong bytes, and a misaligned one is a validation error at bind time, far from the line that declared it.

| Parameter | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `nodeName` | Node that declared the range; named in the message. |
| `handle` | Buffer handle; named in the message. |
| `range` | The declared range. |
| `bufferSize` | Size of the addressed buffer, in bytes. |
| `requiredAlignment` | Device limit for the binding's descriptor type. 1 disables the check. |

**Throws**

- `std::runtime_error` — if the range is zero-sized, out of bounds, or misaligned.

The usage flags an image of this format is created with, before the caller's own are added.

A shared function rather than a line inside one allocator because two paths create images: the engine's resource manager and the graph allocating a transient unbound so it can be bound into a shared block. If those two disagreed about the usage flags, the same declaration would produce two different create infos - which is exactly what the graph's aliasing classes assume cannot happen, since they key an image on its create info.

### `bool Muyo::RenderGraph::FormatSupportsOptimalTilingColorAttachment(VkPhysicalDevice physicalDevice, VkFormat format)`

| Parameter | Description |

### `enum GraphBufferPool`

Which allocation pool a buffer belongs to.

A graph-owned enum rather than the device allocator's PoolType, so the graph can ask for the shader-binding-table alignment without including a device header. VMA's SBT pool exists because a shader binding table's device address must meet shaderGroupBaseAlignment; the caller states the intent and the implementation maps it.

| Value | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `Default` | VMA's default allocation path. |
| `ShaderBindingTable` | Aligned for ray-tracing shader groups. |

### `struct Muyo::RenderGraph::GraphMemoryBlock`

An opaque handle to memory the injected allocator owns.

The graph plans aliasing - which resources share a block and at what offsets - but it does not own the memory. A block therefore crosses the boundary as this handle rather than as a VMA type, and the concrete allocator is the only thing that interprets pImpl. The rest of IGraphResourceAllocator still speaks VmaMemoryUsage, so an implementation does include vk_mem_alloc.h today; the block handle keeps the allocation opaque while that VMA vocabulary remains part of the stated surface.

| Member | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `void * pImpl` | Allocator-private identity; null means "no block". |
| `bool IsNull() const` | Returns: True when this handle names no block. |

### `class Muyo::RenderGraph::IGraphAccelerationStructure`

An acceleration structure the graph can bind and barrier.

A vkCmdPipelineBarrier2 has no barrier type for an acceleration structure, so a queue-family handover is expressed as a buffer barrier on GetBackingBuffer(). That is why the interface exposes the backing buffer and not only the structure handle.

| Member | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `virtual const VkAccelerationStructureKHR & GetAccelerationStructure() const =0` | Returns: The structure handle. |
| `virtual VkDeviceAddress GetDeviceAddress() const =0` | Returns: The device address used to write the structure into a descriptor heap. |
| `virtual VkBuffer GetBackingBuffer() const =0` | Returns: The buffer the structure's memory lives in. |

### `class Muyo::RenderGraph::IGraphBuffer`

A buffer the graph can address, look at and map without knowing whose class it is.

Implemented by the graph's own transients, by the device's VMA-backed resources (VkGraphResourceAllocator) and by the engine's BufferResource, so an imported buffer and a graph-allocated one are the same thing to the barrier, descriptor and binding paths. This is what replaces the graph's old cast to the engine's concrete buffer class: the graph asks a resource what it is instead of asking whether it is one particular engine class.

| Member | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `virtual VkBuffer buffer() const =0` | Returns: The Vulkan buffer handle, or VK_NULL_HANDLE before one has been adopted. |
| `virtual size_t GetSize() const =0` | Returns: The declared size in bytes. |
| `virtual size_t GetCapacity() const =0` | Returns: The allocated capacity in bytes, which is at least GetSize(). |
| `virtual VkBufferUsageFlags GetBufferUsage() const =0` | Returns: The Vulkan usage flags the buffer was created with. |
| `virtual VmaMemoryUsage GetMemoryUsage() const =0` | Returns: The memory usage the buffer was created with. |
| `virtual void * Map()=0` | Map this resource's memory on the host. Returns: A host pointer to the start of its storage, or nullptr when it has none. |
| `virtual void Unmap()=0` | Release a mapping Map took. |
| `virtual void SetData(const void *pData, size_t size)=0` | Upload content into this buffer. Parameters: `pData` - Source bytes, or nullptr to size the buffer without uploading; `size` - Byte count, at most the storage the resource has |

### `class Muyo::RenderGraph::IGraphImage`

An image the graph can barrier, describe and bind without knowing whose class it is.

The image counterpart of IGraphBuffer, and the reason the graph no longer casts to the engine's ImageResource: an imported swapchain image, an engine render target and a graph transient all answer these questions.

| Member | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `virtual VkImage getImage() const =0` | Returns: The Vulkan image handle. |
| `virtual VkImageView getView() const =0` | Returns: The image's view. |
| `virtual const VkImageViewCreateInfo & GetImageViewCreateInfo() const =0` | Returns: The create-info used for the view, for descriptor-heap writes that need its description. |
| `virtual VkFormat GetImageFormat() const =0` | Returns: The image's format. |
| `virtual VkExtent2D GetImageExtent() const =0` | Returns: The image's extent. |
| `virtual VkImageUsageFlags GetImageUsage() const =0` | Returns: The usage flags the image was created with. |
| `virtual uint32_t GetImageMipCount() const =0` | Returns: The created mip level count. |
| `virtual uint32_t GetImageLayerCount() const =0` | Returns: The created array layer count. |

### `class Muyo::RenderGraph::IGraphResource`

The one thing every resource answers: what kind of Vulkan object it is.

The graph's barrier, descriptor and binding paths switch on GetResourceKind() instead of casting to a concrete engine class. The kind is a property of the resource rather than of its C++ type, which is what lets an imported engine resource and a graph-owned transient be handled by the same code.

| Member | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `virtual ~IGraphResource()=default` | Destroy the resource. A consumer-owned resource is destroyed by its owner, not by the graph. |
| `virtual ResourceKind GetResourceKind() const =0` | Returns: The concrete Vulkan object kind behind this resource. |
| `virtual VkObjectType GetVkObjectType() const =0` | Returns: The Vulkan object type, for debug labels and validation messages. |
| `virtual void SetDebugName(const std::string &name) const =0` | Parameters: `name` - Debug name to attach to the Vulkan object |

### `class Muyo::RenderGraph::IGraphResourceAllocator`

What the graph needs from a resource allocator, and nothing more.

The graph owns the policy - transient lifetimes, aliasing, which resource is reused - and receives the mechanism as this interface. muyo_device's VkGraphResourceAllocator is the VMA-backed implementation; a consumer with its own memory manager implements the same interface instead (docs/RenderGraph-Library-Design.md section 4).

Every method is on the allocator rather than on the resource because the graph's transients create a resource unbound, query its requirements, decide the aliasing offsets and only then bind it. A helper that allocated resource and memory together could not do that.

| Member | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `virtual ~IGraphResourceAllocator()=default` | Destroy the allocator. Resources it created must already be destroyed. |
| `virtual std::unique_ptr< IGraphBuffer > CreateBuffer(size_t size, VkBufferUsageFlags usage, VmaMemoryUsage memoryUsage, const std::string &debugName, GraphBufferPool pool=GraphBufferPool::Default)=0` | Create a buffer and the memory it owns. Parameters: `size` - Buffer size in bytes; `usage` - Vulkan buffer usage flags; `memoryUsage` - Intended memory usage; `debugName` - Name used for the Vulkan debug label; may be empty; `pool` - Allocation pool the buffer needs Returns: The buffer, owned by the caller. |
| `virtual std::unique_ptr< IGraphImage > CreateImage(const VkImageCreateInfo &imageInfo, VmaMemoryUsage memoryUsage, const std::string &debugName)=0` | Create an image and the memory it owns. Parameters: `imageInfo` - Image create info, without a memory binding; `memoryUsage` - Intended memory usage; `debugName` - Name used for the Vulkan debug label; may be empty Returns: The image, owned by the caller. |
| `virtual VkBuffer CreateUnboundBuffer(VkDeviceSize size, VkBufferUsageFlags usage)=0` | Create a buffer with no memory bound to it. Parameters: `size` - Buffer size in bytes; `usage` - Vulkan buffer usage flags Returns: The unbound buffer. Destroy it with DestroyUnboundBuffer. |
| `virtual void DestroyUnboundBuffer(VkBuffer buffer)=0` | Destroy a buffer created by CreateUnboundBuffer; its memory belongs to a block. Parameters: `buffer` - Buffer to destroy |
| `virtual VkMemoryRequirements QueryBufferRequirements(VkBuffer buffer) const =0` | Parameters: `buffer` - A buffer created by CreateUnboundBuffer Returns: Its memory requirements. |
| `virtual VkImage CreateUnboundImage(const VkImageCreateInfo &imageInfo)=0` | Create an image with no memory bound to it. Parameters: `imageInfo` - Image create info Returns: The unbound image. Destroy it with DestroyUnboundImage. |
| `virtual void DestroyUnboundImage(VkImage image)=0` | Destroy an image created by CreateUnboundImage; its memory belongs to a block. Parameters: `image` - Image to destroy |
| `virtual VkMemoryRequirements QueryImageRequirements(VkImage image) const =0` | Parameters: `image` - An image created by CreateUnboundImage Returns: Its memory requirements. |
| `virtual GraphMemoryBlock AllocateAliasingBlock(const VkMemoryRequirements &requirements, VmaMemoryUsage memoryUsage)=0` | Allocate memory with no resource bound to it. Parameters: `requirements` - Combined requirements of everything that will alias this block; `memoryUsage` - Intended usage of the block Returns: The block. Free it with FreeAliasingBlock once everything bound to it is destroyed. |
| `virtual void BindBufferToBlock(VkBuffer buffer, GraphMemoryBlock block, VkDeviceSize offset)=0` | Bind an already-created buffer to a byte offset of an aliasing block. Parameters: `buffer` - Buffer to bind; `block` - The block; `offset` - Byte offset inside the block |
| `virtual void BindImageToBlock(VkImage image, GraphMemoryBlock block, VkDeviceSize offset)=0` | Bind an already-created image to a byte offset of an aliasing block. Parameters: `image` - Image to bind; `block` - The block; `offset` - Byte offset inside the block |
| `virtual void FreeAliasingBlock(GraphMemoryBlock block)=0` | Free an aliasing block. Every resource bound to it must already be destroyed. Parameters: `block` - The block to free |
| `virtual void AllocateBuffer(size_t size, VkBufferUsageFlags usage, VmaMemoryUsage memoryUsage, VkBuffer &buffer, GraphMemoryBlock &memory)=0` | Allocate a buffer and the memory it owns, through out-parameters. Parameters: `size` - Size in bytes; `usage` - Vulkan buffer usage flags; `memoryUsage` - Intended memory usage; `buffer` - Receives the buffer; `memory` - Receives the block owning its memory |
| `virtual void FreeBuffer(VkBuffer &buffer, GraphMemoryBlock &memory)=0` | Free a buffer and its memory. Parameters: `buffer` - Buffer to destroy; left as a destroyed handle on return; `memory` - Memory to free; left null on return |
| `virtual void * MapMemory(GraphMemoryBlock block, VkDeviceSize offset=0)=0` | Parameters: `block` - Block to map; `offset` - Byte offset inside the block; zero maps its start Returns: A host pointer to the requested bytes. |
| `virtual void UnmapMemory(GraphMemoryBlock block)=0` | Release a mapping taken by MapMemory. Parameters: `block` - The mapped block |
| `virtual VkImageView CreateImageView(const VkImageViewCreateInfo &createInfo)=0` | Create an image view. Parameters: `createInfo` - View create info Returns: The view. |
| `virtual void DestroyImageView(VkImageView view)=0` | Destroy a view created by CreateImageView. Parameters: `view` - View to destroy |

### `struct Muyo::RenderGraph::ShaderAsset`

One loaded shader: its identity, SPIR-V words, module and reflection.

| Member | Description |
| --- | --- |

| `std::vector< uint32_t > spirv` | The SPIR-V words the module was created from. |
| `VkShaderModule shaderModule` | The module the graph's pipelines use. |
| `Muyo::ShaderReflection shaderReflection` | Reflection of spirv, used to compile descriptors. |

### `struct Muyo::RenderGraph::ShaderAssetKey`

Identity of a loaded shader: its name plus the content it was loaded from.

The name alone is not enough to identify a compiled shader: the .spv file can be rebuilt while the process is running, and a module/reflection pair keyed only on the name would then be served for content it does not match. The content hash makes that a miss instead. It is also what lets a shared cache keep both the old and the new module alive, instead of invalidating a builder that still refers to the old one.

| Member | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `ShaderKey name` | FNV-1a hash of the shader name (no .spv suffix). |
| `uint64_t contentHash` | Hash of the SPIR-V words; see HashSpirv(). |
| `constexpr bool IsValid() const` | Returns: True when both halves name a loaded shader. |
| `constexpr bool operator==(const ShaderAssetKey &other) const =default` | Parameters: `other` - Key to compare Returns: True when both keys name the same content of the same shader. |

### `struct Muyo::RenderGraph::ShaderAssetKey::Hasher`

Hashes both halves of the key for the cache maps.

| Member | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `size_t operator()(const ShaderAssetKey &key) const noexcept` | Parameters: `key` - Key to hash Returns: Hash over the name and content. |

### `class Muyo::RenderGraph::ShaderKey`

FNV-1a hash of a shader's name, used as one half of ShaderAssetKey.

A hash rather than the string keeps the key trivially copyable and cheap to compare; the collision risk is accepted because a collision also has to agree on contentHash to be mistaken for a hit.

| Member | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `uint32_t Value` | The stored hash type. |
| `constexpr ShaderKey()=default` | Construct the zero (invalid) key. |
| `constexpr ShaderKey(std::string_view s)` | Parameters: `s` - Shader name, without the .spv suffix |
| `constexpr Value GetValue() const` | Returns: The hash. |
| `constexpr bool operator<(const ShaderKey &rhs) const noexcept` | Parameters: `rhs` - Key to compare Returns: True when this key sorts before rhs; required for std::map. |
| `constexpr bool operator==(const ShaderKey &rhs) const =default` | Parameters: `rhs` - Key to compare Returns: True when both keys hold the same hash. |
| `constexpr bool IsValid() const` | Returns: True when this key names a shader rather than the default-constructed zero. |

### `struct Muyo::RenderGraph::ShaderKey::Hasher`

Hashes a ShaderKey for the std::unordered_map used by the caches.

| Member | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `size_t operator()(const ShaderKey &key) const noexcept` | Parameters: `key` - Key to hash Returns: Its hash. |

### `struct Muyo::RenderGraph::RenderGraphTrace`

One execution of a compiled graph, as data.

Read-only by construction: it is derived from CompiledRenderGraph's const accessors and never written back. It is a value, not a view over the graph - the graph is rebuilt every frame, consumers keep history, and out-of-process consumers need something they can serialise and diff.

Three layers live in one object, and only the first is populated today:

structural: nodes, segments, transfers, dependency edges and barriers; temporal: TraceSegment::gpu and the host intervals - reserved, valid == false; derived: occupancy, bubbles and critical path are computed by consumers from the two above.

| Member | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `uint32_t schema` | Wire format version of the serialised form. A format version, not the library's version: a bump is a compatibility statement to tools, not to linkers. |
| `uint64_t execution` | Execution counter; engine-lifetime, not per-frame. |
| `TraceScope scope` | Device and topology that produced this trace. |
| `std::vector< TraceNode > nodes` | Every compiled node, in compiled order. |
| `std::vector< std::size_t > cpuNodes` | Host-side nodes, which run before any GPU segment. |
| `std::vector< TraceSegment > segments` | GPU segments, in execution order. |
| `std::vector< TraceSignal > signals` | Timeline values signalled, filled at submit. |
| `std::vector< TraceWait > waits` | Waits, filled at submit. |

### `struct Muyo::RenderGraph::TraceBarrier`

One barrier recorded inside a segment, in the forms a reader can interpret.

Stages and accesses are stored as names, not bitmasks: a reviewer or a model reading EARLY_FRAGMENT can act on it, where 0x100 is a puzzle. The mask itself is not carried - the trace is for reading, and the barrier is re-derivable from the uses.

| Member | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `ResourceHandle resource` | Resource the barrier addresses; empty for a device-wide memory barrier. |
| `TraceBarrierKind kind` | Which kind of barrier this is. |
| `std::string srcStage` | Source stage mask, rendered by NameOfPipelineStages. |
| `std::string dstStage` | Destination stage mask. |
| `std::string srcAccess` | Source access mask, rendered by NameOfAccesses. |
| `std::string dstAccess` | Destination access mask. |
| `VkImageLayout oldLayout` | Layout the image is in before the barrier; UNDEFINED for a buffer or memory barrier. A first use with oldLayout == UNDEFINED discards the resource's contents, so an imported image that was meant to keep them is visible here as the difference between its stated layout and UNDEFINED. |
| `VkImageLayout newLayout` | Layout the use needs. UNDEFINED for a buffer or memory barrier. |
| `uint32_t srcFamily` | Source family for a handover, IGNORED otherwise. |
| `uint32_t dstFamily` | Destination family for a handover, IGNORED otherwise. |

### `enum TraceBarrierKind`

Which kind of barrier a recorded barrier is.

An enum rather than a const char* because the first version used a bare pointer, and comparing it with == against a literal silently compared two const char* values from different translation units - which is exactly the kind of quiet false negative this record exists to prevent.

| Value | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `Image` | VkImageMemoryBarrier2. |
| `Buffer` | VkBufferMemoryBarrier2, including an acceleration structure's backing buffer. |
| `Memory` | Device-wide VkMemoryBarrier2; addressed to no single resource. |

### `struct Muyo::RenderGraph::TraceEdge`

An ordering constraint between two segments, with its cause.

The cause is the point: a dependency without the resource that forces it is a fact nobody can act on, and it is free to record where the barrier or handover is derived.

| Member | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `std::size_t from` | Segment that must complete first. |
| `std::size_t to` | Segment that must wait. |
| `ResourceHandle resource` | Resource forcing the order; empty for QueueOrder. |
| `TraceEdgeKind kind` | Why the order exists. |

### `enum TraceEdgeKind`

Why one segment must run after another.

| Value | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `Transfer` | A resource is handed over across a queue-family boundary. |
| `QueueOrder` | Both segments submit to the same queue, so program order already orders them. |

One field of the serialised object: its key, and what renders its value.

The table exists so the field list is data. The JSON emitter walks it, and a test asserts every key appears in the output, so a struct member that is added without being emitted fails the suite instead of quietly missing from the contract.

| Member | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `const char * name` | JSON key. |
| `std::string(* render` | Renders the value, already JSON-encoded. |

### `struct Muyo::RenderGraph::TraceInterval`

A time range recorded for a segment or a host-side node.

Reserved and unfilled in the structural trace. Every interval is invalid until timestamps are collected (#56 phase 2), and valid is what distinguishes "this took no time" from "nobody measured it" - a zero would read as instantaneous to anything consuming the trace. The field is present from the first version so the recorded shape does not change when the measurements arrive.

| Member | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `bool valid` | True once a begin and an end were measured. |
| `uint64_t beginNs` | Nanoseconds, scaled from ticks at the edge. Meaningless when !valid. |
| `uint64_t endNs` | Nanoseconds, scaled from ticks at the edge. Meaningless when !valid. |

### `RenderGraphTrace Muyo::RenderGraph::TracePlan(const RenderGraphExecutionPlan &plan, std::span< const TraceNodeView > nodes, const TraceScope &scope)`

Build the structural part of a trace from a plan and the compiled nodes it refers to.

Device-free: the plan carries segments and transfers, and the views carry names and queues, so a test can build the same record a device would without creating one. Dependency edges are derived here with their causes - a transfer for each cross-family handover, program order for consecutive segments on one queue.

| Parameter | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `plan` | Plan the executor will run. |
| `nodes` | Compiled nodes the plan indexes, in compiled order. |
| `scope` | Device and topology producing this trace; nothing is queried from it. |

**Returns** — The structural trace, with every temporal field still invalid.

### `struct Muyo::RenderGraph::TraceScope`

What produced a trace and what it can therefore be compared against.

A trace that does not name its device and topology can be quoted outside the configuration it describes - the same failure mode [test device] exists to prevent for test runs.

| --- | --- |
| `std::string deviceName` | VkPhysicalDeviceProperties::deviceName. |
| `uint32_t graphicsFamily` | Queue family running graphics work. |
| `uint32_t computeFamily` | Queue family running async compute work. |
| `bool bDedicatedCompute` | False when there is one family, so no async compute at all. |
| `uint32_t inFlightCount` | Executions that may be in flight at once. |
| `TraceTimestamps timestamps` | What can be timed on these queues. |

A contiguous run of compiled nodes that executes on one queue, as recorded.

### `struct Muyo::RenderGraph::TraceTimestamps`

Timestamp capability of the queues a trace ran on.

Recorded so a trace states its own scope: a run whose queue family has no timestamps, or whose compute and graphics timestamps are not comparable, cannot be quoted as if it did.

| `uint32_t validBitsCompute` | Same for the compute family; 0 means that lane is unmeasurable. |
| `double periodNs` | timestampPeriod: nanoseconds per tick. |
| `bool bSharedDomain` | True when compute and graphics timestamps share one clock domain. |
| `bool bCalibrated` | True when host and GPU clocks were aligned for this execution. |
| `bool bKnown` | False in the structural trace: nothing has been queried yet. |

## `ShaderCache.h`

### `class Muyo::RenderGraph::ShaderCache`

A caller-owned cache of loaded shader modules and their reflection results, shared across builders.

RenderGraphBuilder loads a shader from RenderGraphServices::shaderSource (by default shaders/<name>.spv), creates a VkShaderModule and runs SPIR-V reflection while the graph is declared. Without this cache each builder repeats that work for the same shader, and the modules live only as long as that builder. Inject one through RenderGraphServices::shaderCache to share both:

A hit creates no module and runs no reflection. It returns the identity of the entry already in the cache, so two builders resolve the same VkShaderModule and the same reflection object. The key is the shader name plus a hash of its SPIR-V words (ShaderAssetKey), not the name alone: a .spv rebuilt while the process runs is a different shader, and serving the old reflection for it would compile a pipeline for content that is no longer there. Both entries stay alive, because a builder may still refer to the old one. The cache owns the modules. A builder never destroys a module it did not create, and a module may be destroyed after the pipelines created from it (Vulkan allows this), but a later Build() needs it again, so the cache's lifetime is what keeps it valid.

Lifetime. Device-scoped, and it must outlive every builder that uses it. Destroy it only after those builders are gone (or at least after their last Build()); no entry is refcounted.

LoadShader() still asks the shader source for the words to identify their content, even on a hit. The save is the module creation and reflection, which are the expensive parts; a caller that wants to avoid the source lookup as well would need a content identity supplied from outside, which is not this contract.

Threading. One thread at a time, like the builder and the caches it uses. The map is not synchronized.

| Member | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `ShaderCache(VkDevice device)` | Parameters: `device` - Device the shader modules are created on. Must not be VK_NULL_HANDLE, and has to outlive the cache: destroying a module needs the same device Throws: `std::runtime_error` - when device is VK_NULL_HANDLE |
| `~ShaderCache()` | Destroy every module this cache created. No builder may still resolve an entry through it. |
| `ShaderCache(const ShaderCache &)=delete` | Owns Vulkan handles and destroys them, so copying would double-destroy a module. |
| `ShaderCache & operator=(const ShaderCache &)=delete` | Deleted for the same reason as the copy constructor. |
| `ShaderCache(ShaderCache &&)=delete` | Deleted because a moved-from cache would leave the old object with no modules to destroy. |
| `ShaderCache & operator=(ShaderCache &&)=delete` | Deleted for the same reason as the move constructor. |
| `std::optional< ShaderAssetKey > LoadShader(const std::string &shaderName)` | Load shaders/<shaderName>.spv, or return the identity of the entry already cached for it. Parameters: `shaderName` - Shader name without the .spv suffix, as RenderGraphNodeCreateInfo names it Returns: The entry's key, or std::nullopt when the source has no words or the module cannot be created. Throws: `std::runtime_error` - when the file cannot be read; that is the same failure a builder without a shared cache reports |
| `std::optional< ShaderAssetKey > LoadShader(const std::string &shaderName, const IShaderSourceProvider &source)` | Load shaderName from source, or return the identity of the entry already cached for it. Parameters: `shaderName` - Shader name without the .spv suffix; `source` - Provider of the shader's SPIR-V words. Must outlive the call; the words are copied into the cache on a miss Returns: The entry's key, or std::nullopt when the source has no words or the module cannot be created. Throws: `std::runtime_error` - when the source throws; the default file provider does so for a file that cannot be read |
| `const ShaderAsset * GetShaderAsset(const ShaderAssetKey &key) const` | Parameters: `key` - Key returned by LoadShader Returns: The module, SPIR-V words and reflection for key, or nullptr when it is not cached. |
| `std::size_t GetModuleCount() const` | Returns: How many shader modules the cache currently owns. |
| `std::uint64_t GetModuleCreateCount() const` | Returns: How many modules the cache has created over its lifetime (its misses). A second builder loading the same shaders leaves this unchanged; tests use it as the reuse evidence. |
| `VkDevice GetDevice() const` | Returns: The device the modules were created on, so a builder can reject a cache from another one. |


## `ShaderSourceProvider.h`

### `class Muyo::RenderGraph::FileShaderSourceProvider`

The default shader source: reads <searchPath>/<shaderName>.spv from the filesystem.

This reproduces the graph's historical behaviour when searchPath is left at its default of "shaders". Supplying one with a different path is how a host points the graph at its own shader directory without implementing IShaderSourceProvider:

constFileShaderSourceProvidershaderSource("build/shaders"); RenderGraphBuilderbuilder(RenderGraphServices{ .device=device,.resourceAllocator=&allocator,.shaderSource=&shaderSource});

Missing and empty files. A file that cannot be opened throws std::runtime_error("Failed to open file"); a file of zero bytes yields std::nullopt. Both are the behaviour ReadSpirvFile and the graph had before this provider existed.

| Member | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `FileShaderSourceProvider(std::filesystem::path searchPath="shaders")` | Parameters: `searchPath` - Directory the .spv files are read from. A relative path is resolved against the process's working directory, not the source tree, at every load |
| `~FileShaderSourceProvider() override=default` | Destroy the provider; it owns only the path. |
| `std::optional< std::vector< uint32_t > > LoadShader(const std::string &shaderName) const override` | Read <searchPath>/<shaderName>.spv. Parameters: `shaderName` - Shader name without the .spv suffix Returns: Its words, or std::nullopt when the file is empty. Throws: `std::runtime_error` - when the file cannot be opened or read, or is not a whole number of 32-bit words |
| `const std::filesystem::path & GetSearchPath() const` | Returns: The directory this provider reads from. |

### `class Muyo::RenderGraph::IShaderSourceProvider`

Where the graph gets a shader's SPIR-V from (#292).

Every shader a node declares is loaded during AddNode(). With no provider in RenderGraphServices::shaderSource the graph reads shaders/<shaderName>.spv from the process's working directory, which is what every in-tree consumer does. A host with no .spv files - an embedded runtime, a compiler that produces the words in memory, a test - implements this interface and passes it in RenderGraphServices::shaderSource; the graph then asks it for the words instead of opening a file.

The provider is host-owned. The graph neither copies nor destroys it: it must outlive every builder that refers to it, and every ShaderCache call that is given it. LoadShader() returns the words by value, so their lifetime is the caller's from the moment the call returns.

Threading. The builder is single-threaded, so a provider is called from one thread at a time for a given builder. A provider shared by builders on different threads has to synchronise itself. LoadShader() is const because it is a lookup; a provider that memoizes its answer keeps that cache in mutable state or builds it before the first call.

Failure modes. An implementation returns std::nullopt for a name it does not have, and may also return an empty vector for that case. The graph turns either into its named Node 'N declares shader 'S', which could not be loadederror. An exception thrown from LoadShader()propagates out ofAddNode()(the default file provider throws std::runtime_error("Failed to open file")for a missing file, as the graph did before the provider existed). Non-empty words that are not valid SPIR-V are not rejected by this interface: reflection or module creation fails, either by throwing or by making the load returnstd::nullopt`.

| Member | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `virtual ~IShaderSourceProvider()=default` | Destroy the provider. The host owns it and must keep it alive while a builder refers to it. |
| `virtual std::optional< std::vector< uint32_t > > LoadShader(const std::string &shaderName) const =0` | Return the SPIR-V words for a shader name. Parameters: `shaderName` - The name a node declared, without the .spv suffix, exactly as it appears in RenderGraphNodeCreateInfo::shaderNames or rtShaderNames Returns: The shader's SPIR-V words (one uint32_t per word), or std::nullopt when no shader of that name exists. An empty vector is accepted as the same answer. Throws: `std::runtime_error` - (or any other exception) to report a failure that is not a missing entry; it propagates out of the AddNode() or ShaderCache::LoadShader() call |


## `TransientMemoryPlan.h`

### `struct Muyo::RenderGraph::TransientMemoryBlock`

One allocation, and the slots laid out inside it.

One block per compatibility class, because a block is one VkDeviceMemory-sized unit: everything in it is bound to the same memory, which is what makes its class a contract rather than a label.

| Member | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `TransientMemoryClass classKey` | The class every member of every slot belongs to. |
| `VkDeviceSize size` | Bytes to allocate: the end of the last slot. |
| `VkDeviceSize alignment` | Alignment to allocate with: the maximum over all slots. |
| `uint32_t memoryTypeBits` | Memory type bits to allocate with: the intersection over all members. Zero is an error, reported by PlanTransientMemory rather than left for the allocator to fail on. |
| `std::vector< TransientMemorySlot > slots` | The slots, in offset order. |

### `struct Muyo::RenderGraph::TransientMemoryClass`

The compatibility class a transient's memory belongs to.

Two transients may share one block exactly when their classes compare equal, so the class is the aliasing contract, stated once and checkable: a buffer and an image never share a block, and two images share one only when their create info is identical.

Identical create info is deliberately stricter than Vulkan requires. Aliasing two images whose formats differ is legal only with VK_IMAGE_CREATE_ALIAS_BIT and only when the formats are in the same compatibility class, and those rules are a table to get wrong from memory. Requiring the create info to match removes the question instead of answering it, and the cost - memory left on the table when two images differ only in format - buys the invariant "same class, therefore safe", which is true by construction rather than by consulting a table at every plan.

A buffer's class carries no shape fields, because every buffer may share memory with every other buffer: the constraints that exist for images come from format compatibility and from tiling, and a buffer has neither.

One field is not shape and belongs here anyway: memoryTypeBits. Two resources whose allowed memory types are disjoint cannot share memory whatever their shape, and the case is reachable rather than theoretical - a buffer created CPU_ONLY and one created GPU_ONLY have disjoint type sets on a discrete device, and both are ordinary. Carrying the bits in the class keeps the planner total: such a pair lands in two blocks instead of producing a plan the allocator cannot satisfy, and the intersection check inside the planner becomes the safety net for a caller that built the class by hand rather than the mechanism for telling them apart.

| Member | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `VkFormat format` | Pixel format, for images. Unused for buffers. |
| `VkExtent2D extent` | Image extent, for images. Unused for buffers. |
| `uint32_t mips` | Mip level count, for images. Unused for buffers. |
| `uint32_t layers` | Array layer count, for images. Unused for buffers. |
| `VkImageUsageFlags usage` | Image usage flags, for images. Unused for buffers. |
| `uint32_t memoryTypeBits` | Memory type bits the device allows for this resource, from its memory requirements. |
| `VmaMemoryUsage memoryUsage` | The memory usage its block will be allocated with. A block is one allocation, so everything in it is created with one usage - and two resources asking for different usages are asking for different contracts even when the device offers them the same memory types. |
| `bool isImage` | True for images, false for buffers. The discriminator: a buffer's other fields are all defaults. |
| `bool operator==(const TransientMemoryClass &other) const` | Parameters: `other` - Class to compare against Returns: True when two transients may share a block. |
| `bool operator<(const TransientMemoryClass &other) const` | Parameters: `other` - Class to compare against Returns: A strict weak ordering, so classes can key a map. It orders blocks in the plan deterministically; it carries no meaning about memory. |

### `struct Muyo::RenderGraph::TransientMemoryPlan`

What a build's transients should do with memory: one block per class, one offset per non-overlapping group.

| Member | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `std::vector< TransientMemoryBlock > blocks` | One per class that has any transient. Empty when the graph has no transients. |
| `VkDeviceSize reservedBytes` | Bytes the graph will allocate: the sum of the blocks' sizes. |
| `VkDeviceSize individualBytes` | Bytes it would allocate with one resource each: the sum of the requests' sizes. The two numbers together are the whole point - see SharesMemory. |
| `std::size_t SlotCount() const` | Returns: How many distinct offsets the plan reserves across all blocks. |
| `bool SharesMemory() const` | Returns: True when the plan allocates less than one resource each, i.e. some slot is shared. False is a legitimate answer for a graph whose transients all overlap; it is not a failure, and a caller that reports it as one would be reporting on its own graph. |

### `struct Muyo::RenderGraph::TransientMemorySlot`

One offset inside a block, shared by every member whose live range does not overlap another's.

| Member | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `std::vector< ResourceHandle > members` | Resources bound at this offset. Never two whose intervals overlap - that is the plan's promise. |
| `VkDeviceSize offset` | Offset from the start of the block. |
| `VkDeviceSize size` | Bytes reserved here: the largest member's size, aligned up to the widest member's alignment. |
| `VkDeviceSize alignment` | The widest member's alignment. The offset above is a multiple of it. |
